background.text: [0001] This invention is in the field of valves, as it relates to the use of unified geometric control - line, triangle, square, cross, circle, and curvature elements - for the design and operation of a. [0002] Conventional valves products address only isolated aspects of their task. A product may optimize one parameter while leaving geometry, decision branching, and tolerance flow to ad-hoc design choices made late in development, when change is most expensive. The result is a Check valve whose parts fit by adjustment rather than by design. [0003] Geometry in conventional practice is handled by general-purpose drafting or modeling tools that record shape without recording intent. When a dimension shifts, there is no single origin to re-solve from, so tolerance stack-ups accumulate silently across interfaces and the Check valve drifts from its rated POWER of 247.4 W. [0004] Decision branching in conventional valves products is typically hard-coded: operating modes, configuration paths, and fallback behaviors are fixed at build time. When conditions change, the Check valve cannot re-derive its own behavior because the branching was never expressed as a solvable structure. [0005] Further, conventional builds produce no machine-readable record of what was decided and why. Verification depends on human-readable documents that drift from the built article, so two units built to the same drawing can differ in behavior without any detectable trace. [0006] There remains a need for a that collapses shape, rule, and dimension into one controlled origin and re-expands through six defined tools, that expresses branching as solvable geometry, and that emits a machine-readable build record with every unit.

summary.text: SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [0007] The present invention provides a forced through a universal reverse reduction algorithm. The Check valve comprises six-tool mapped elements wherein LINE, TRIANGLE, SQUARE, CROSS, CIRCLE, and CURVATURE jointly define the Check valve, key parameters including POWER of 247.4 W and WEIGHT of 73.8 g, and a machine-readable autoread block ending STATUS=SIGNATURE-1 VALID. [0008] It is an object of the invention to provide: (a) a single solvable origin from which all geometry of the Check valve is re-derivable; (b) line-path control of primary dimension axis along the check valve; (c) triangle-hierarchy control of taper and load angle of the check valve structure; (d) square-bound control of bounding enclosure of the check valve; (e) cross-branch decision control of junction points where check valve subassemblies cross; (f) circle-node anchoring of circular features: ports and mounts of the check valve; and (g) curvature-flow shaping of fillet and bend radii across the check valve housing. [0009] It is a further object to express every operating decision of the Check valve as a reversed allowance path: seed the Signature-One grid to anchor the Check valve as a binary-1 identity, set the finished function as the destination on the infinite line and back-solve, route the target through the six tools, admit human variance in perspective, chance, and tolerance slop, and emit the Check valve as one valid build among infinite option paths. [0010] In one embodiment the Check valve is configured to operate at POWER of 247.4 W and WEIGHT of 73.8 g, within IP_RATING of IP65, and the autoread block records the as-built parameters with each unit. In alternative embodiments the six tools are re-weighted for past, current, or future operating eras without changing the origin.

abstract.detailed: A Check valve for valves is disclosed. The Check valve unifies six geometric control tools - line paths, triangle hierarchies, square bounds, cross branches, circle nodes, and curvature flow - in a single solvable origin, and forces every build decision through a reversed universal allowance algorithm, so that geometry, decision branching, and tolerance flow are designed together instead of being left to ad-hoc choice. In one embodiment the Check valve (10) comprises a control core (100) coupled to a line-path module (110) governing primary dimension axis along the check valve, a triangle hierarchy unit (120) governing taper and load angle of the check valve structure, a square bound frame (130) bounding bounding enclosure of the check valve, a cross decision branch (140) deciding junction points where check valve subassemblies cross, a circle node anchor (150) anchoring circular features: ports and mounts of the check valve, and a curvature flow shaper (160) shaping fillet and bend radii across the check valve housing. The control core (100) is further coupled to an autoread block (170) that emits a machine-readable record of the build ending STATUS=SIGNATURE-1 VALID. In operation the Check valve runs five reversed-allowance steps in order - universal-bit starter, reverse-target, combinatorial mix, human variance, and multi-path solved reality - to yield the Check valve at POWER of 247.4 W and WEIGHT of 73.8 g, with the geometry of every step traceable through the six tools.

technical.field_statement: [0001] This invention relates to valves, and more particularly to a with unified six-tool geometry control through a reversed universal allowance algorithm.
technical.description_numbered: [0011] Referring to FIG. 1, one embodiment of the Check valve (10) is constructed by collapsing all shape, rule, and dimension into one controlled origin and re-expanding through the six tools. A control core (100) anchors the origin and sequences the five reversed-allowance steps. [0012] The control core (100) holds the binary-1 identity seeded at universal-bit starter (310): a single declared origin from which every downstream dimension is derived, so that no geometry exists without a recorded parent decision. [0013] The line-path module (110) governs primary dimension axis along the check valve. All linear extents, alignments, and signal or load paths of the Check valve are projected from the origin through the line-path module, which fixes direction before magnitude. [0014] The triangle hierarchy unit (120) governs taper and load angle of the check valve structure. Layered dependencies - primary, secondary, and tertiary functions of the Check valve - are stacked as triangle hierarchies so that a change at the apex propagates deterministically to the base. [0015] The square bound frame (130) bounds bounding enclosure of the check valve. The operating envelope of the Check valve is enclosed in square bounds that define hard limits; nothing in the design may cross a bound without triggering a re-solve from the origin. [0016] The cross decision branch (140) decides junction points where check valve subassemblies cross. Operating modes and configuration paths are expressed as cross branches - explicit, solvable forks rather than hard-coded switches - so the Check valve re-derives its behavior when conditions change. [0017] The circle node anchor (150) anchors circular features: ports and mounts of the check valve. Reference nodes of the Check valve are fixed as circle anchors: radial datums that hold position while surrounding geometry flexes within tolerance. [0018] The curvature flow shaper (160) shapes fillet and bend radii across the check valve housing. Transitions between states, surfaces, or phases of the Check valve follow curvature flow, eliminating sharp discontinuities that would otherwise concentrate stress, error, or loss. [0019] Referring to FIG. 2, the Check valve is rated at POWER of 247.4 W and WEIGHT of 73.8 g. The parametric diagram plots the two against each other within IP_RATING of IP65; the shaded envelope marks the region in which all six tools remain inside their square bounds. Operation outside the envelope forces a re-solve rather than a silent drift. [0020] The autoread block (170) emits, for each built unit, a machine-readable record of the as-built parameters, the tool mapping, and the five algorithm steps, terminated by STATUS=SIGNATURE-1 VALID. Two units built to the same origin carry comparable records, so behavioral drift is detectable without human-readable documents. [0021] Referring to FIG. 3, the reversed universal allowance algorithm begins at universal-bit starter (310): the Signature-One grid is seeded to anchor the Check valve as a binary-1 identity, establishing the single origin. [0022] At reverse-target (320), the finished function of the Check valve is set as the destination on the infinite line and the design is back-solved toward the origin, so every intermediate decision is justified by the destination it serves. [0023] At combinatorial mix (330), the target is routed through the six tools - line paths, triangle hierarchies, square bounds, cross branches, circle nodes, curvature flow - and each tool claims the geometry that belongs to it, with conflicts resolved by re-solving from the origin. [0024] At human variance (340), perspective, chance, and tolerance slop are admitted in the execution of the Check valve: the design holds its rated POWER of 247.4 W while tolerating the real-world variation of builders, operators, and environments. [0025] At multi-path solved reality (350), the Check valve is emitted as one valid build among infinite option paths - the path that satisfies the destination, the six tools, and the tolerance band together. [0026] In operation, the control core (100) sequences steps (310)-(350) in order for each build or operating session of the Check valve, then verifies the autoread block (170) before release. A failed verification returns the Check valve to reverse-target (320) rather than shipping a drifted unit. [0027] Means of manufacture follow the six-tool sequence: source materials to print tolerance, form the primary structure, fit interfaces and seals, assemble subassemblies, finish and protect surfaces, and run calibration and QA burn-in with the autoread block stamped on the unit. [0028] Alternative embodiments re-weight the six tools for past, current, or future operating eras: a past-era embodiment favors proven line and square geometry; a future-era embodiment favors cross-branch adaptability and curvature flow. The origin and the five steps are unchanged. [0029] The invention is not limited to the embodiments described. Any apparatus that collapses shape, rule, and dimension into one controlled origin, re-expands through the six defined tools, and emits the machine-readable build record falls within the scope of the appended claims.

how_it_works: Start with one controlled origin point - the 'binary-1' anchor - so the whole Check valve grows from a single known-good spot.
Aim at the job it must do and work backwards, which locks the power of 247.4 W target before any material is cut.

Run the design through six shapes: lines for primary dimension axis along the check valve, triangles for taper and load angle of the check valve structure, squares for bounding enclosure of the check valve, crosses for junction points where check valve subassemblies cross, circles for circular features: ports and mounts of the check valve, and curves for fillet and bend radii across the check valve housing.
Allow human-style slack - perspective, chance, tolerance - so the Check valve works in the real world, not just on paper.
Output the finished Check valve as one valid build, with a machine-readable autoread block stamped on it for verification.
